hints: Write the first row and column from zero: they form 0,1,2,... .
Compare the first few rows with bitwise XOR.
The cell at one-based (y,x) equals (y-1) XOR (x-1).
analogy: Each row is the first row rearranged by toggling the bits of its row index.
example: At (2,3), zero-based coordinates are 1 and 2; 1 XOR 2 is 3.
algorithm: For each query subtract one from the row and column indices and print their bitwise XOR.
correctness: In row r, values r XOR c for c before x are distinct, and in column x, values r' XOR x for r' before r are distinct. Every number smaller than r XOR x appears to the left or above by flipping its highest differing bit; the current value appears in neither, so it is the mex.
complexity: For q queries, O(q) time and O(1) extra space using fixed-width integers.
